cards.title: Diagnose wrong-audience targeting through three observable signals
cards.summary: Missed response, high visitor-to-customer gap, and buyers leaving mid-evaluation are symptoms of mismatched audience targeting.
cards.use_when: Auditing organic or paid traffic that arrives but does not convert, or reviewing whether content is written for the wrong searcher.

cards.title: Measure organic add-to-cart, checkout and purchase in GA4 to find funnel leaks
cards.summary: Compare ecommerce event counts period-over-period, filtered to organic search, to find which funnel step is dropping.
cards.use_when: Reviewing whether organic traffic is producing revenue, or diagnosing whether a traffic decline is actually a conversion problem.

cards.title: Find and fix high-bounce pages by exporting first, prioritising second
cards.summary: Export bounce rate by page path across channels, skip checkout pages, and prioritise outdated or thin content first.
cards.use_when: Running a content refresh sprint, or deciding which pages deserve rewriting versus leaving alone.

cards.title: Use impressions vs clicks to find pages that rank but fail to attract
cards.summary: High-impression, low-click pages reveal title, description or UX problems, not ranking problems.
cards.use_when: Deciding whether to improve page titles and meta descriptions, or whether a page's problem is content depth versus click-through.

cards.title: Create and submit an XML sitemap as a bridge to search engines
cards.summary: XML sitemaps are for crawlers; HTML sitemaps are for people, and the source treats XML as the mandatory one for new stores.
cards.use_when: Launching a new store, adding a large batch of new pages, or finding that new URLs are not being indexed.

cards.title: Fix page speed and Core Web Vitals using Search Console's diagnostic drill-down
cards.summary: Use Core Web Vitals reports in Search Console to find slow or unstable pages, then hand developers specific asset-level fixes.
cards.use_when: Diagnosing a high bounce rate tied to slow pages, or prioritising technical work that affects ranking and conversion.

cards.title: Limit flash and heavyweight elements so crawlers can index the page
cards.summary: Flash and very heavy media elements make pages slow, unindexable and unappealing, and should be used sparingly if at all.
cards.use_when: Reviewing an existing storefront's homepage or campaign landing page for heavy embeds and old technology.

cards.title: Pogo-sticking: use SERP returns to judge whether your page answers intent
cards.summary: Google reads users bouncing back from your result to another as evidence of irrelevance, so visit-to-result alignment is a ranking input.
cards.use_when: Reviewing why a well-optimised page sits below weaker competitors, or understanding non-converting organic sessions.

cards.title: Optimise for branded (navigational) searches you should already own
cards.summary: Branded query performance is treated as reputation management — you should be the first result for your own brand name.
cards.use_when: Auditing branded search performance, deciding whether to invest in brand-term pages, or comparing your branded click share to a competitor's.

cards.title: Compete on original, current content rather than copied product copy
cards.summary: Original, regularly refreshed content is the source's stated defence against ranking decay, especially in categories where manufacturers supply identical descriptions.
cards.use_when: Writing collection and product copy on a store that carries manufacturer-supplied descriptions, or planning content maintenance.

cards.title: Use eye-tracking and click-tracking principles to shape UX that converts
cards.summary: Users scan rather than read, so design the top band to hold attention and instrument the actions you want them to take.
cards.use_when: Reviewing a storefront, category page or landing page for whether it sustains attention long enough for the visitor to buy or subscribe.

cards.title: Use social media as an adjacent channel that feeds brand search
cards.summary: Social profiles are a visible trust layer on the site and a place to publish current offers; over-marketing without relevance destroys the benefit.
cards.use_when: Planning promotional calendars for a store or deciding whether to invest in profiles and content beyond the site.

cards.title: Avoid black hat SEO that produces short-lived rankings and penalties
cards.summary: Keyword stuffing, arbitrary pages and other unethical shortcuts are detected within months and downgrade the site.
cards.use_when: Choosing between a fast ranking tactic and a sustainable one, or reviewing an inherited SEO strategy for risky practices.

cards.title: Choose the right keywords before worrying about traffic volume
cards.summary: Wrong keyword selection sends you outside the box entirely — keyword, audience and content must be chosen in that order.
cards.use_when: Selecting target terms for a new store's category pages, or re-evaluating why a keyword strategy is not producing conversions.

cards.title: Teach yourself to read a live SERP before writing a page
cards.summary: Inspecting the actual results for your target query shows what format and what level of detail is already winning.
cards.use_when: Before creating a category page, collection page or product landing page, or when diagnosing why a page is outranked.

cards.title: Audit Flash and JavaScript bloat as page-experience obstacles
cards.summary: Treat obsolete Flash embeds and unused or glitchy JavaScript as indexing and speed barriers to clean up on an ecommerce storefront.
cards.use_when: Running a technical SEO audit on your storefront's page experience before paid traffic or a redesign push.

cards.title: Confirm your store already has an auto-generated XML sitemap instead of building one
cards.summary: Modern CMS platforms auto-generate XML sitemaps, so verify and submit the existing one rather than generating sitemaps manually.
cards.use_when: Setting up technical SEO for a new store on Shopify, WordPress, or another CMS, especially with hundreds or thousands of product pages.

cards.title: Match sitemap type to audience: XML for crawlers, HTML for shoppers
cards.summary: XML sitemaps feed search bots while HTML sitemaps help human navigation, and each carries a different SEO role.
cards.use_when: Deciding which sitemap to expose when structuring store navigation, a large category tree, or orphaned product pages.

cards.title: Use Ahrefs keyword difficulty filters to find rankable store keywords
cards.summary: Filter keyword lists by volume and difficulty (KD 0–40) to find terms a new or small store can realistically rank for.
cards.use_when: Choosing which product, category or content keywords to target for a new or low-authority ecommerce store.

cards.title: Mine question keywords and filter by KD when planning store content
cards.summary: Question-based informational keywords reveal what shoppers ask, and filtering to low difficulty helps new stores rank for them.
cards.use_when: Planning blog, guide or FAQ content that supports an ecommerce store's SEO and attracts early-stage shoppers.

cards.title: Assess competitor authority and SERP features before choosing a keyword
cards.summary: Check who already ranks and whether AI overviews or People Also Ask appear before deciding a keyword is worth pursuing.
cards.use_when: Deciding whether a target product or content keyword is realistically winnable for your store.

cards.title: Choose a content format matched to the query and buyer stage
cards.summary: Listicles, how-to guides, blogs, video, opinion pieces and infographics each serve different search intents and commercial purposes.
cards.use_when: Deciding what format to publish for a store's content calendar — category education, product guides or brand-building.

cards.title: Apply personalization and localization to store content and offers
cards.summary: Personalization uses shopper details to prioritise relevance; localization targets the right message to the right region at the right time.
cards.use_when: Adapting PDP copy, offers or messaging for specific regions, languages or returning customers.

cards.title: Read engagement, bounce and conversion metrics by page in GA4
cards.summary: Use engagement rate, bounce rate and ecommerce purchase data at page level to find which store pages hold attention and drive purchases.
cards.use_when: Diagnosing which product, blog or landing pages hold shoppers and which lose them, as a basis for content and PDP improvements.

cards.title: Spot declining pages by comparing active users period over period
cards.summary: Export page-level traffic for two periods and subtract to surface pages losing users so you can prioritise their recovery.
cards.use_when: Monthly ecommerce content and SEO review to find PDPs, category pages or blog posts that are losing organic traffic.

cards.title: Install GA4 by adding the measurement tag to the site head
cards.summary: Create a GA4 property, place the Google tag in the head, then verify installation in real time.
cards.use_when: Setting up analytics on a new or redesigned storefront so you can see traffic, behaviour and ecommerce revenue.

cards.title: Size the SEO opportunity with GA4 channel comparison
cards.summary: Compare organic channel users and sessions across two periods to see whether SEO is growing or slipping.
cards.use_when: Reporting store SEO performance to stakeholders or deciding whether to invest more in organic content.

cards.title: Create and verify a Google Business Profile for local store discovery
cards.summary: A verified Google Business Profile places your store in maps and local packs, which matters for local and mobile searchers.
cards.use_when: Setting up or improving local SEO so nearby shoppers can find your store or service area.

cards.title: Use Google Search Console for crawl issues and indexing health
cards.summary: Search Console complements analytics by surfacing crawl errors, 404s and indexing status that GA4 does not show.
cards.use_when: Investigating why store pages are not being indexed or why organic impressions diverge from your expectations.

cards.title: Use engagement and conversion metrics to diagnose shopper fit
cards.summary: Click-through rate, time on page and conversion rate are the user-behaviour signals the source highlights for SEO and commercial performance.
cards.use_when: Judging whether a store page is performing and deciding what to improve on a landing page or PDP.

cards.title: Plan visually with mapping tools, but build strategy from competitor analysis
cards.summary: Visual site-mapping tools help structure a store's pages and keywords, but the source insists strategy comes from human analysis of competitors, not tool output alone.
cards.use_when: Planning a store's information architecture, category tree or keyword map before a build or migration.

cards.title: Prioritise low-difficulty, high-volume terms over vanity head keywords
cards.summary: The source's core keyword principle: pick terms with good volume and low difficulty so a store can gain visibility rather than chasing unwinnable head terms.
cards.use_when: Deciding which terms to target for a new store or a new category where you currently have no ranking.

cards.title: Reference the sitemap in robots.txt to control crawling and discovery
cards.summary: robots.txt hides unwanted pages from crawlers and can also point crawlers to your sitemap, combining exclusion and discovery in one file.
cards.use_when: Configuring a store's robots.txt after launch or a site migration so Google crawls product pages but skips non-indexable URLs.

cards.title: Treat canonical URLs as the single version of each store page
cards.summary: Canonical URLs identify the single preferred version of a page's content, preventing duplicate versions from splitting ranking signals.
cards.use_when: Reviewing a store with filter, pagination or parameter variants that create near-duplicate product URLs.

cards.title: Understand where SEO tracking tools fit before wiring them up
cards.summary: GA4, Search Console and Tag Manager are the three core tracking pillars the source recommends for SEO measurement, feeding audits, meta tags and event tracking.
cards.use_when: Planning the tracking stack for a new store or auditing gaps before running SEO and conversion experiments.

cards.title: Prepare store content for AI-assisted and voice search
cards.summary: Search is shifting toward AI overviews, People Also Ask and voice, which changes how content should be written and how page speed is assessed.
cards.use_when: Planning content and page experience for a store that wants visibility in AI overviews and voice assistant results.

cards.title: Edit permalinks to keep product and post URLs short and specific
cards.summary: Long title-based URLs are discouraged; custom permalinks let you shorten and specify the URL for a page.
cards.use_when: Publishing a new product, category or blog page where the default URL would be a long version of the title.

cards.title: Set follow/nofollow deliberately when building internal links
cards.summary: Dofollow links pass ranking opportunity while nofollow links do not; the default is dofollow and should be reserved for pages you want to strengthen.
cards.use_when: Adding internal links between product pages, categories and blog content, or managing outbound links on a store.

cards.title: Set Up Google Search Console for a Store Property
cards.summary: Install and verify Search Console using the exact HTTPS URL-prefix property, and place the verification tag in the site head.
cards.use_when: Onboarding a new store domain or taking over a Shopify/WooCommerce/custom site and you need crawling, indexing and query data before diagnosing traffic.

cards.title: Find High-Impression Low-Click Queries in Search Console
cards.summary: Sort Search Console queries by impressions to surface ranking pages that fail to earn clicks, then diagnose relevance, position and load time.
cards.use_when: Monthly SEO triage for a store: deciding which category, collection or blog pages need new titles, content or speed work.

cards.title: Compare Two Periods to Isolate Which Pages Lost Clicks
cards.summary: Use Search Console period comparison plus an exported Google Sheet with a difference formula to rank pages by click and impression decline.
cards.use_when: When store traffic drops after a site change, season shift or algorithm update and you need to name the specific pages that lost the most visibility.

cards.title: Audit Indexing Coverage and Fix 404s and No-Indexed Pages
cards.summary: Use Search Console Indexing to separate intentionally excluded dynamic URLs from genuine broken product and collection URLs, then repair only the meaningful ones.
cards.use_when: Cleaning up a store's crawl budget and recovering link equity after category, product or URL-structure changes.

cards.title: Install Google Tag Manager and Deploy Analytics Through It
cards.summary: Set up a GTM web container, fire GA4 through a constant variable so code lives outside the theme, and verify the tag with Preview mode.
cards.use_when: When a store wants to add or change tracking tags (analytics, pixels, schema, event tracking) without editing theme code for every change.

cards.title: Create and Validate Articles/Blog Schema for Rich Snippets
cards.summary: Generate article-type schema from a template tool, fix validation warnings (typically date format), and never deploy unchecked code.
cards.use_when: Preparing blog or buying-guide content for rich results, or planning product-page schema such as star ratings and FAQ blocks.

cards.title: Fire Page-Specific Schema from Google Tag Manager
cards.summary: Deploy schema per URL via GTM with a page-path trigger so each blog post or FAQ page carries its own markup without theme edits.
cards.use_when: When content teams cannot touch the CMS templates but need structured data on specific blog, FAQ or product pages.

cards.title: Read an Ahrefs-Style Domain Rating and Backlink Profile
cards.summary: Interpret DR, UR, backlinks, referring domains, organic keywords and traffic as a comparative profile rather than a target score.
cards.use_when: Benchmarking a store against competitors before deciding whether link building, content or on-page work deserves the next sprint.

cards.title: Compare Ranking Position Over Time to Find Lost and Declined Keywords
cards.summary: Export the keyword table, split it into top-3/4-10/11-20 buckets and compare periods to build a fix list of declined and lost terms.
cards.use_when: Quarterly keyword triage: identifying product or category searches the store used to rank for and has slipped away from.

cards.title: Attribute Traffic Loss to Specific Pages Using Peak-Period Comparison
cards.summary: Compare today's traffic and top pages against a known good month to name the pages responsible for a decline, including zero-traffic pages that still load.
cards.use_when: When total organic traffic is falling and you need to separate pages that lost rankings from pages that merely lost clicks.

cards.title: Judge Backlink Quality with Referring Domains, DR and Spam Score
cards.summary: Sort backlinks by domain rating, inspect self-created zero-authority and nofollow links, and screen domains for spam before deciding to disavow.
cards.use_when: Reviewing a store's inbound link profile after outreach or a link-building campaign, and cleaning up toxic links.

cards.title: Run an Ahrefs Site Audit and Prioritise Errors by Colour
cards.summary: Crawl the store and work red errors before yellow warnings, fixing 404s, canonical mismatches, orphan pages, http links and oversized images with developer support.
cards.use_when: Setting up a recurring technical audit for a store, particularly before or after a replatform or URL restructure.

cards.title: Write Meta Titles and Descriptions Inside the CMS Within Length Limits
cards.summary: Fix title and description length warnings by editing the CMS record, targeting roughly 60 characters for titles and 140-160 for descriptions.
cards.use_when: Clearing yellow audit warnings on product, collection and blog pages, and improving click-through from search results.

cards.title: Write and Place Alt Text for Store Images
cards.summary: Add concise, descriptive alt text (3-4 words) to product, blog and template images so Google can interpret them, using the CMS or a developer for template-level images.
cards.use_when: Clearing missing/empty alt text warnings on product images, blog imagery and shared footer icons.

cards.title: Use Semrush Keyword Gap to Find Competitor Terms You Are Missing
cards.summary: Compare your ranking keyword set with a competitor's and subtract the common terms to size the untapped opportunity before adding anything.
cards.use_when: Planning content or category expansion and deciding which competitor-driven keywords are safe and relevant to pursue.

cards.title: Track Add-to-Cart and Button Click Events Without Back-End Code
cards.summary: Use Google Tag Manager event tracking to count clicks on submit and add-to-cart buttons instead of requesting developer instrumentation.
cards.use_when: Store analytics phase where you need button-level engagement data for PDPs, forms or checkout-adjacent CTAs.

cards.title: Set up Add-to-Cart event tracking with Google Tag Manager without touching site code
cards.summary: Use GTM Preview mode to identify a button's click text, then create a GA4 click-trigger tag to log add-to-cart events and build a checkout funnel view.
cards.use_when: You want to measure how many shoppers click Add to Cart (or Checkout/Purchase buttons) on your product pages but don't want to edit the store's backend code.

cards.title: Diagnose where shoppers drop off in the add-to-cart-to-purchase flow
cards.summary: Once add-to-cart, checkout and purchase click events are logged in GA4, compare counts across the three steps to locate the biggest funnel leak.
cards.use_when: You suspect shoppers abandon between cart and checkout or between checkout and payment, and want data on which stage loses the most people before deciding where to optimize.

cards.title: Keyword Magic Tool: seed keyword to qualified opportunity list
cards.summary: Use Semrush's Keyword Magic Tool to expand one seed keyword into a filtered list of rankable keywords with intent, volume and difficulty.
cards.use_when: Starting keyword research for a product category or content plan and you need a prioritized list of realistic ranking targets before briefing content or product pages.

cards.title: AI Prompt Research: what customers ask ChatGPT and AI search
cards.summary: Use Semrush's Prompt Research to see the questions buyers ask AI tools on your topic, which brands get mentioned, and which sources AI cites.
cards.use_when: Deciding whether your brand appears in AI answers for buying-intent questions, and which prompts to target with content or PDP copy.

cards.title: Competitor Organic Rankings: read their organic playbook
cards.summary: Use Organic Rankings to see every keyword a competitor ranks for, their SERP features, and how their keyword mix by intent shifts over time.
cards.use_when: Merchandising or content planning when you want to understand which topics and intents a direct competitor is winning and where they are exposed.

cards.title: Keyword Gap: find keywords competitors rank for and you don't
cards.summary: Use Keyword Gap to surface keywords your competitors rank for (Missing) or where you rank far lower (Weak), and convert them into target lists.
cards.use_when: Building a content or category-page roadmap where you want to close specific ranking gaps against named competitors.

cards.title: Cluster your keyword list into a content calendar
cards.summary: Use Keyword Strategy Builder to consolidate keyword lists and auto-cluster them so each cluster becomes one page or piece of content.
cards.use_when: Turning a scattered keyword list into a concrete monthly content or category-page plan with defined primary intent per page.

cards.title: Topic Research: headlines and questions that already work
cards.summary: Use Topic Research to find proven headlines and audience questions around a topic so you write from evidence instead of a blank page.
cards.use_when: Planning blog or category-page content when you need headline angles and questions that already resonate before briefing a writer.

cards.title: SEO Writing Assistant: score and fix a draft before publishing
cards.summary: Use Semrush's SEO Writing Assistant to score a draft against target keywords and fix readability, title length and originality issues before publication.
cards.use_when: Reviewing a finished or near-finished product description, blog post or landing page copy before it goes live.

cards.title: Site Audit: fix errors first, warnings second
cards.summary: Run a Site Audit to find technical errors that block crawling and ranking, then work through issues in priority order rather than chasing a perfect score.
cards.use_when: Before a content or merchandising push, when you need to confirm product and category pages are crawlable and not returning errors.

cards.title: robots.txt and llms.txt: crawlability for Google and for AI
cards.summary: Add both robots.txt and llms.txt so traditional crawlers and AI bots can find and prioritize your most important pages.
cards.use_when: When Site Audit reports pages blocked from AI search, or when launching or restructuring a store and want AI tools to surface your key pages.

cards.title: Backlinks overview: authority, best links and lost links
cards.summary: Use the Backlinks overview to assess referring-domain quality and recover high-value lost links rather than chasing raw link counts.
cards.use_when: When planning link building or diagnosing a drop in domain authority and organic visibility for a store.

cards.title: Backlink Gap: find sites linking to competitors but not you
cards.summary: Use Backlink Gap to list referring domains that link to multiple competitors but not to you, filtered by authority, as an outreach checklist.
cards.use_when: Planning outreach to earn links and AI-cited authority in your niche, especially when competitor roundups or listicles already exist.

cards.title: Position Tracking: monitor Google rankings and AI summaries together
cards.summary: Set up Position Tracking with your priority keywords so you can watch rank changes and AI-summary appearances over time in one view.
cards.use_when: After publishing new content or making technical fixes, to verify movement and catch visibility changes early.

cards.title: Domain Overview: catch declining traffic and visibility trends
cards.summary: Use Domain Overview to see overall SEO and AI-search visibility in one place and spot negative trends early.
cards.use_when: Doing a periodic health check on your store's organic and AI visibility, or diagnosing a suspected traffic decline.

cards.title: AI Visibility Overview: which LLMs mention and cite you
cards.summary: Use the AI Visibility Overview to quantify brand mentions across ChatGPT, Google AI, Perplexity and Gemini, and see where to focus AEO effort.
cards.use_when: Deciding which AI platform to prioritize for AEO work, or reporting brand presence in AI answers to stakeholders.

cards.title: Brand Performance: how ChatGPT talks about you and what to fix
cards.summary: Use Brand Performance to see sentiment, share of voice, business drivers and prioritized strategy recommendations for how AI describes your brand.
cards.use_when: Setting AEO and brand-messaging priorities when you need to know how AI assistants position you versus competitors for buying-intent questions.

cards.title: The four-step search loop: research, organize, fix, track
cards.summary: Follow Semrush's four-step workflow — research Google and AI demand, cluster it into a content plan, fix site and backlink gaps, then track results and repeat.
cards.use_when: Setting up or resetting an ongoing SEO/AEO program for a store and you need an ordered operating sequence rather than ad hoc tasks.

cards.title: Keyword Research Workflow with Google Keyword Planner and Trends
cards.summary: Build a per-page keyword set (one main, two supporting) using Google Keyword Planner volume/CPC data and Google Trends related queries.
cards.use_when: Planning keyword targets before editing a homepage, product page, collection, or blog post's SEO fields.

cards.title: Separate Informational vs Transactional Search Intent
cards.summary: Match keywords to intent so product and collection pages target buyers while blog posts absorb informational searches.
cards.use_when: Deciding whether a keyword belongs on a product/collection page, a blog post, or nowhere in your catalog.

cards.title: Edit Global Store SEO: Homepage Title and Meta Description
cards.summary: Set the site-wide homepage title and meta description so the homepage ranks for your main brand/category keyword.
cards.use_when: Setting or fixing the homepage listing that appears in Google results for brand and category searches.

cards.title: Enforce a Single H1 Tag Per Page
cards.summary: Ensure every page has exactly one H1 so Google can identify the page's main topic.
cards.use_when: Auditing a theme or custom section for heading structure on product, collection, homepage, or custom-built pages.

cards.title: Write SEO Product Titles from Specs Using Keyword Data
cards.summary: Turn raw product specs into a keyword-rich but readable product title and description.
cards.use_when: Rewriting vague product names (e.g., 'Sweet Honey Bomb') that don't tell Google or shoppers what the product is.

cards.title: Image SEO: Alt Text, File Names, and Formatting
cards.summary: Optimize every product/media image with descriptive alt text and a keyword-based file name.
cards.use_when: Preparing product photos, banners, and gallery media before or after uploading to Shopify.

cards.title: Write Product Meta Descriptions That Earn Clicks
cards.summary: Craft a roughly 160-character product meta description focused on click appeal rather than keyword density.
cards.use_when: Filling the per-product Search engine listing meta description field in Shopify.

cards.title: Clean URL Handles and Enable 301 Redirects
cards.summary: Shorten product/collection URL handles and keep the automatic redirect checked to avoid losing bookmarked traffic.
cards.use_when: Editing a product or collection URL handle in the Search engine listing preview.
